kicker: Whole-disk search, read end to end

scenes.headline: How a Mac finds any file in a millisecond
scenes.sub: One crawl, one mapped file, and a very cheap filter.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Rummage! Noah Dunnagan built a tool that finds any file on a Mac by name in about a millisecond. Here's how.

scenes.text: Store each distinct file name once, and put a filter that costs a single AND in front of the real matcher.
scenes.mark: a filter that costs a single AND
scenes.say: The trick isn't a clever index. Store each distinct name once, and put a filter costing one AND in front of the matcher.

scenes.title: From the disk to a ranked list

steps.say: One parallel crawl reads every folder, sizes and times included, into a single file the daemon maps into memory.
A query tests every distinct name against a mask of the letters it contains. Most names fail right there.
Survivors meet the fuzzy scorer, and matching names fan back out to files.
When the kernel says a folder changed, fsearch lists it again and diffs it.

parts.note: letter classes the query has and the name lacks
parts.say: Take the letter classes the query has and the name lacks.
If nothing is missing, score it. A typo may miss one class, if a word starts with the right letter.

scenes.title: Why not a trigram index for names?

left.title: Trigram index
items: Needs three letters in a row
A typo leaves nothing to look up
left.say: A trigram index needs three letters in a row. A typo leaves nothing to look up.

right.title: Mask, then scan
items: One typo forgiven at a word start
right.say: A mask and a scan over distinct names handles typos, and is fast enough.

scenes.credit: Noah Dunnagan's launch demo, final frame
scenes.title: What the big ratio compares

steps.say: The launch line says seventeen thousand times faster than Finder. The chart compares against fd, which walks the whole disk every search.
That's an index beating a crawl, not one index beating another.

scenes.title: Name search on a Chromium checkout
scenes.note: median of 1,500 queries, the project's own benchmark
scenes.say: Against fff, the project's own benchmark has fsearch about thirteen times faster on a big tree.

scenes.text: Score distinct names, filter with one AND before the expensive matcher, and lay folders out so a subtree is one range.

recap: Crawl once, then diff changed folders
The big ratio is against a crawl
scenes.say: Crawl once, let one AND reject most names, and read the big ratio as an index beating a crawl.
